title: Singular genitive: frequent special stems
summary: Learn these four frequent forms as word-and-stem pairs: lapsi (“child”) → lapsen.
objectives: Learn these four frequent forms as word-and-stem pairs: lapsi (“child”) → lapsen.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: The genitive is a case form. It can link a word to an owner or another noun. Here you practise the word form; later lessons show its uses in sentences.
Learn these four frequent forms as word-and-stem pairs. Each has a change that a simple final-letter rule would miss.
keyPoints: Learn the word with its stem; the last letter alone does not identify every pattern.

steps: Use the stem lapse-: lapsi → lapse-; add -n to get lapsen.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Use the special stem miehe-: mies → miehe-; add -n to get miehen.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Use the stem velje-: veli → velje-; add -n to get veljen.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Use the weak stem poja-: poika → poja-; add -n to get pojan.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.

commonMistakes: Learn the word with its stem; the last letter alone does not identify every pattern.
Keep the requested number: singular is one, plural is more than one.
A slash between model forms marks accepted alternatives; write just one form.

practiceExercises.prompt: Complete the singular genitive of lapsi (“child”): lapse____. Write only the missing letter.
practiceExercises.explanation: Use the stem lapse-: lapsi → lapse-; add -n to get lapsen.

practiceExercises.prompt: Complete the singular genitive of mies (“man”): ____n. Write only the letters before the final n.
practiceExercises.explanation: Use the special stem miehe-: mies → miehe-; add -n to get miehen.

practiceExercises.prompt: Practise the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: poika (“boy”); veli (“brother”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Use the weak stem poja-: poika → poja-; add -n to get pojan. Use the stem velje-: veli → velje-; add -n to get veljen.
